mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only: director's signature notarized by a Hong Kong notary public, then the notarial certificate is apostilled by the High Court Registry; consular legalization is not employed.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only: notarized by a Hong Kong notary public, then apostilled by the Hong Kong High Court Registry; no consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Conduct mandatory risk-based screening of every UBO, shareholder, director, legal representative, senior manager, authorized signatory and connected close associate against: OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists; UN Security Council Consolidated List; EU consolidated financial sanctions lists where relevant; PRC lists of persons and entities subject to UN Security Council resolutions; domestic disciplinary and integrity records. Apply PEP rules covering foreign PEPs, domestic prominent public officials at or above county or deputy department level, senior state-owned enterprise executives and international organization officials. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory when a PEP is identified: verify source of wealth and funds, obtain senior management approval, perform continuous transaction monitoring, and retain records for at least five years. Adverse media and negative news screening must be documented and escalated to the AML/CFT compliance officer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) and SAMR enterprise name self-service declaration portal; local acceptance by the Shanghai Municipal Administration for Market Regulation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must be in standard Simplified Chinese and must follow the four-tier structure: administrative division, distinctive trade name of at least two Chinese characters, industry or business characteristic reflecting electric cargo bicycle manufacturing, and the organizational form Limited Liability Company. The foreign investor's name may be transliterated into Chinese and adopted as the trade name. Latin-script names, pinyin and English trade names are auxiliary only and are not the registered legal name; the Chinese name governs for tax, customs and banking filings.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, obtain the written rejection notice and the precise statutory ground. If the rejection is based on identical or misleading similarity, file an administrative reconsideration with the municipal or provincial SAMR within 60 days of receipt, or bring an administrative lawsuit within six months. In parallel, resubmit a new name declaration after removing the offending token or after obtaining the required ministerial approval for any sensitive term. The appeal must be submitted in Simplified Chinese with the filing code, rejection notice, applicant identity certificate and, where applicable, trademark or prior-use evidence. Reconsideration must be decided within 60 days; failure to decide may itself be challenged in court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an ISIC 3091 electric cargo e-bike manufacturer, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the sole registered address. PRC Company Law and SAMR registration rules require the registered address to be the principal place of business; the tax authority requires a physical production address for VAT invoice control, export tax refunds and enterprise income tax verification; PBOC supervisory practice and Chinese banks generally reject corporate account opening at a

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 July 2024), Articles 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 23, 24, 32, 33, 34, 41 and 47; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020), Articles 2, 4, 5, 6, 13 and 28; Regulations on Foreign Investment Information Reporting (Ministry of Commerce Order No. 2, 2019); and Regulations on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (State Council Decree No. 746, 2022), Articles 9 to 20.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - Enterprise Registration and Credit Supervision Department, acting through the local Municipal or District Administration for Market Regulation where the WFOE registered office is located.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Company Establishment Registration Form, together with the Articles of Association, name reservation notice, investor qualification documents and registered address certificate, all submitted through the SAMR enterprise registration online service window.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None - no statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a wholly foreign-owned enterprise engaged in non-restricted manufacturing under the current PRC Foreign Investment Law and Company Law, and no blocked escrow account rule applies. The company may adopt a subscribed registered capital regime; the first contribution is due within the period stated in the Articles of Association and the entire subscribed capital must be paid in within five years of establishment. The Hong Kong shareholder's contribution must be remitted through the foreign exchange capital account and cannot be released for any purpose outside the approved business scope.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS IN WRITING OF THE SOLE SHAREHOLDER AND FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN WFOE LTD (the Company), adopted contemporaneously with the execution of the Articles of Association on ____. WHEREAS, the Company is to be incorporated as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise under the laws of the People's Republic of China, with ISIC 3091 business scope comprising the design, manufacture, assembly, testing, sale and after-sales service of electric cargo bicycles, step-through scooters, related traction batteries and components; WHEREAS, the sole shareholder has subscribed for the entire registered capital and intends to fund initial working capital through the foreign exchange capital account; and WHEREAS, the Company requires a registered office, banking relationships and statutory officers to conduct its affairs. NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS RESOLVED THAT: 1. Capital Subscription. The registered capital of the Company is fixed at USD ____, divided into ____ ordinary shares of equal nominal value, and the sole shareholder hereby subscribes for all such shares. The first tranche of not less than ____ percent of the subscribed capital shall be paid into the Company's capital contribution account within ninety days after issuance of the business license, and the balance shall be paid in full not later than five years from incorporation, in accordance with Article 47 of the PRC Company Law. No escrow account is required by law, but no capital may be withdrawn except for lawful operating purposes and with all necessary foreign exchange approvals. 2. Banking Authorization. The Company shall open a basic RMB deposit account

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China via the national Electronic Taxation Bureau (e-Tax) portal for the mainland WFOE; in Hong Kong SAR, the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) is the competent authority for profits tax and Business Registration under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), using the official eTAX platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: The foreign investor forms the WFOE with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); the SAMR-issued business license contains the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the statutory taxpayer identification number (TIN) for all PRC tax purposes. Step 2: Within 30 days of license issuance, log into the Electronic Taxation Bureau with the USCC to complete initial tax filing status, report the WFOE registered address, shareholders, directors, and bank account, and obtain the VAT classification (general taxpayer or small-scale taxpayer). Step 3: Enrol in the Golden Tax IV digital invoice system for VAT special and ordinary invoices, and if the WFOE is exporting goods, register as an export-tax-rebate taxpayer with the local STA export rebate section and obtain customs export registration through the China International Trade Single Window. Step 4: Register under the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) Goods-Trade Foreign Exchange Control system so that export proceeds can be reported and matched to the export declarations. Step 5: A foreign non-resident shareholder or Hong Kong parent without a permanent establishment in mainland China does not obtain a separate PRC TIN; the WFOE will withhold PRC taxes at source and the non-resident must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence from the Inland Revenue Department of Hong Kong (or its home jurisdiction) and provide its Hong Kong Business Registration Certificate number as the foreign tax identifier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. PRC law does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch pass-through election for a WFOE; the WFOE is mandatorily taxed as a resident enterprise at entity level. Available statutory elections are limited to the VAT general-taxpayer election (mandatory once annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000), the small-scale taxpayer method below that threshold, and the High and New Technology Enterprise election for a 15% CIT rate where qualification is met. Hong Kong does not offer a U.S.-style check-the-box election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China (PRC VAT), including the export VAT zero-rate/rebate system and the digital e-invoice clearance regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 in annual taxable sales for mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration; any WFOE with taxable business must obtain tax registration immediately upon business license issuance, and a WFOE may voluntarily register as a general VAT taxpayer before reaching the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices are subject to the State Taxation Administration Golden Tax Phase IV platform: they must be created as fully digitalised e-invoices or machine-printed fiscal invoices carrying a unique control number, encrypted digital seal, QR code, and anti-fraud features, and must be uploaded to the STA e-Tax invoicing database in near-real time. For export rebate purposes, the electronic invoice data must be reconciled with the China Customs export declaration through the China International Trade Single Window; no paper-only invoice can substantiate zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The WFOE may claim 0% VAT on exported electric cargo bicycles and step-through scooters when the goods are sold to an overseas buyer, physically leave the China Customs territory, the WFOE is the legal exporter with valid VAT and export rebate registration, the export declaration matches the VAT invoice and sales contract, and the export proceeds are repatriated to China within 180 days of export. Qualifying offshore digital services (e.g. firmware or telematics supplied to non-resident customers and wholly consumed outside China) may also be zero-rated where separate cross-border service documentation is maintained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (the electronic export goods declaration matched through the China International Trade Single Window)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill or equivalent multimodal transport document
Commercial export invoice and detailed packing list
Export sales contract or purchase order with Incoterms
Bank-issued Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) / export proceeds repatriation certificate supported by the SAFE Goods-Trade Foreign Exchange Collection Report
VAT special invoices for input-credit substantiation and the VAT export invoice/ordinary invoice required by the STA export rebate system
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: STA and Customs audit zero-rating claims by cross-matching Golden Tax IV invoice data, Single Window customs data, SAFE foreign-exchange receipt data, bank statements, and logistics records. If the export zero-rating is false, unsupported, or proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days, the STA will reverse the zero-rate and rebate, assess unpaid VAT, apply a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day from the original refund date, and impose an administrative fine of one to five times the fraudulently obtained refund under Article 66 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Tax Administration and Collection; tax evasion penalties under Article 63 range from 50% to five times the evaded amount. Criminal liability for fraudulent export tax refunds may be referred, and recovery limitation periods are unlimited for fraudulent claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), the foreign exchange administrative body under the People's Bank of China (PBOC), is the binding central FX authority for the mainland WFOE; the Hong Kong Monetary Authority governs clearing channels and offshore renminbi liquidity for the HK parent treasury
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The WFOE operates under the mainland Chinese foreign exchange control regime, which is materially different from Hong Kong's free convertibility. Current account items, including trade settlement, service fees and profit remittances, are generally convertible after genuine transaction verification and SAFE filing. However, capital account operations remain strictly controlled. Injection of equity capital from the Hong Kong parent into the WFOE requires an FDI registration certificate issued by SAFE, disbursement in accordance with the approved foreign exchange capital account and an actual-use conversion restriction (no purely speculative conversion or intra-group lending without SAFE approval). Profit remittance to the Hong Kong shareholder is permitted only after the WFOE has completed annual audits, filed corporate income tax returns, obtained tax clearance and passed bank-level payment verification. In practice, an onshore RMB shortage, customs declaration mismatches or deficiencies in the SAFE Form FDI-1 and related true-transaction documents will delay outflow clearance. The currency, while RMB, is not fully convertible for capital-account purposes; all cross-border transfers of substance require documentary corroboration by both the onshore branch and the HK banking correspondent.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE Circular 28 and the 2019 reform measures, there is no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds; a WFOE may retain foreign exchange in an onshore foreign currency settlement account or convert to RMB at will. Statutory repatriation generally requires delivery of the foreign currency into the onshore settlement account within 90 days from the date of export declaration or as stipulated by the customs/trade credit regulations; longer collection cycles must be pre-registered with SAFE as offshore trade credit or by the bank as an exceptional trade-finance arrangement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI platforms, including Wise Business, Revolut Business, Airwallex and MultiPass, are not licensed to operate as deposit-taking or clearing members inside mainland China and cannot open or maintain onshore RMB settlement accounts for a WFOE. The mainland WFOE must transact through a licensed domestic CBRC/CSRC-regulated bank to satisfy SAFE reporting, capital account verification and RMB cross-border clearing. The Hong Kong parent treasury may lawfully use an EMI for pre-bank aggregation of customer e-bike pre-payments or short-term corporate spending, but the EMI cannot be a substitute for, or directly feed, the onshore WFOE's bank account. Legal viability for onshore use is therefore low-to-nil.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mainland Chinese banks require the WFOE's legal representative and at least one board-authorized KYC officer to attend a physical onboarding interview at the designated branch in China. A remote consular proxy or fully virtual account opening is not accepted for a first-time WFOE relationship; the HK parent's directors do not need to appear physically, provided the onshore legal representative presents original HK parent company documents, notarized board resolutions and the apostilled certificate of incumbency, followed by a due-diligence call or video meeting with the HK parent's authorized signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in the Hong Kong shareholding chain and use of nominee directors or low-tax HK shelf companies without audited substance; the bank flags beneficial-ownership excavation risk under HK's Company Ordinance and mainland CDD rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled certificate of incorporation and current commercial registry search; full organizational chart and UBO declaration extending to natural persons; HK Inland Revenue Department business registration certificates; audited financial statements of the HK parent for the last two fiscal years; statutory declarations from nominee shareholders resigning or confirming trust status; bank references from the HK parent's existing relationship bank; and source-of-wealth evidence for the ultimate individual investors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital account injection funded from third-party remittance accounts, crypto-flat conversions, or a commingled offshore treasury pool rather than the registered shareholder's banking account, raising money-laundering and round-tripping suspicion under SAFE anti-avoidance rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FDI Registration Certificate (SAFE Form FDI-1) with the exact quota matched to the remittance; certified letter of authorization from the HK parent's board approving the specific capital transfer; bank statements covering the originating account in the HK parent's name showing the complete funding trail from profit reserves, intra-group loans or external borrowing; legalized share subscription agreement; notarized passport/corporate ID copies of all signatories; and a formal written explanation of any commingled treasury sweeps, supported by the offshore accounting ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering indicators in the electric cargo e-bike export cycle, including overpricing of battery or motor purchases, repeated invoice values that deviate from industry benchmarks, phantom logistics for dense charged cells, or African/Latino end-destination routing without clear end-user identification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete transaction repository for each export/import leg: purchase orders and signed master contracts; customs export declarations with HS codes; unique logistics waybills; packing lists; CMR/sea waybills or e-airway bills; insurance certificates; original manufacturer VAT invoices for lithium battery cells, chargers and motor units; third-party price benchmarking or independent cargo surveyors' valuation; and proof of physical inventory sampling by customs-broker.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, dual-use component exposure or diversion risk on high-capacity battery systems and intelligent drive controllers, particularly where the HK parent is used as a bill-to/from intermediary for shipments to sanctioned or uncertain jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Restricted-party screening log from a continuously updated global sanctions aggregator (OFAC, EU, HM Treasury, HK Customs and UN); final destination and end-user certificates from each overseas customer; contractual insertion of an export control clause prohibiting re-export to embargoed states; technical specification sheets demonstrating non-military classification of the e-bike drive train; and the WFOE's internal export compliance manual with management sign-off.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Hong Kong parent must execute a SWIFT MT103 from its fully funded corporate account to the WFOE's onshore FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account held at the designated Tier-1 Chinese bank. The beneficial owner and remitter fields must match the SAFE-registered shareholder, not third parties. The remittance information must contain the SAFE FDI registration number, the WFOE's unified social credit code, and the precise purpose code 'Capital Injection - Foreign Investor Purchasing Registered Capital' or equivalent SAFE code, together with the wording 'Equity Investment into WFOE for Production Capacity Construction'. The Chinese RMB receiving bank will verify the registration certificate, confirm the payment falls within the paid-in limit, then credit the capital account in FX or convert to RMB under the 'actual-need' principle. A certified Chinese CPA must subsequently issue a capital verification report evidencing receipt of the registered paid-up capital before the WFOE applies for operational funding conversion.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Direct current-account payments to overseas suppliers (battery cells, display controllers, torque sensors, hub motors) should be executed via SWIFT MT103 or locally issued letters of credit through the onshore bank's trade finance desk. Commercial letters of credit (irrevocable at sight, payable in USD or RMB) are the preferred clearing rail for high-value components, with the presentation of packing list, commercial invoice, bill of lading and China Compulsory Certification (CCC) test reports. Documentary collections (documents against payment / documents against acceptance) may be used for established low-risk suppliers; all outbound FX payments require genuine transaction contracts and customs evidence to avoid SAFE penalty. For intra-group royalties, engineering services or management fee flows to Hong Kong, an MT103 with tax-withholding certificate and SAFE current-account filing is necessary.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB/USD forward contracts issued by licensed Chinese banks, only for maturity-matched trade or capital-servicing exposure booked under the SAFE risk-need test.
Cross-currency swaps between RMB and HK dollars or USD where the notional matches a registered onshore import/export contract and is evidenced at each rollover using customs declarations.

RMB/USD non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts on the CNH deliverable only in the Hong Kong offshore market and only for the HK parent's retransfer exposure; mainland WFOE cannot legally book an onshore NDF as a speculative overlay.
FX swap and options combinations limited to real demand, with a prohibition on leveraged or naked speculative positions; all hedge documentation must be renewable against current SAFE trade filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: PRC Enterprise Annual Information Report to the State Administration for Market Regulation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January through 30 June of each year for the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by 30 June places the WFOE on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations; if unresolved for three consecutive years, the entity is moved to the List of Seriously Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprises, triggering cross-department credit restraints, restrictions on government procurement, banking, tax refunds, and visas, and possible administrative revocation of the business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Information Annual Report (FDI Annual Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and local commerce authorities, transmitted through the SAMR National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January through 30 June of each year for the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The commerce authority orders correction within 20 days; if the WFOE refuses or fails to correct, an administrative fine of RMB 100,000 to RMB 500,000 may be imposed, along with publication of the violation in the national credit record and loss of preferential foreign investment treatment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Settlement and Payment Filing (CIT Annual Filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) and local competent tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of the following calendar year for the preceding tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest accrues at 0.05% per day on unpaid tax; failure to file on time attracts a fine of up to RMB 2,000 in ordinary cases and RMB 10,000 in serious cases; false filing or concealment of income may result in an administrative penalty of 50% to five times the evaded tax, criminal liability for tax evasion, and tax credit blacklisting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Related-Party Transactions Report and Transfer Pricing Documentation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) and local competent tax authority, submitted with the CIT annual return package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of the following calendar year for the annual related-party transaction report; contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation must be prepared on or before 31 December of the tax year and delivered on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false filing may trigger a transfer-pricing audit, deemed-profit adjustment, late-payment interest and additional interest components, administrative fines under the Tax Collection Administration Law, and stronger exposure to 50%-to-500% penalty assessments on under-declared tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Annual Audited Financial Statements and Audit Report Approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting and board of directors; audited statements must be available to SAMR, MOFCOM, and the STA on demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual audit report must be issued within four months after the financial year-end and in any event before the 31 May CIT annual settlement deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to procure a PRC-licensed statutory audit may result in Company Law liability, rejection of loss carry-forward claims and tax concessions, failure of the foreign investment annual report, regulatory inquiry, and adverse credit records.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Above-Scale Industrial Enterprise Annual Statistical Report (conditional if annual main business revenue exceeds RMB 20 million)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) and local statistics bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual statistical reporting window generally runs from 1 January through 31 March of the following year; exact local notice applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Untrue or delayed statistical declarations can attract fines under the PRC Statistics Law of up to RMB 200,000 for serious violations, inclusion in the enterprise credit supervision system, and administrative liability for the legal representative.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Social Insurance Contribution Base Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau (HRSSB) and the social insurance collection arm of the tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Usually announced each July for the upcoming contribution year; the exact annual declaration must be filed within the local notice period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late declaration or underpayment triggers a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day, administrative fines, restriction on credit access, legal representative accountability, and possible denial of government subsidies or export preferences.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the PRC Company Law, every PRC limited-liability company, including a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise, must have its annual financial statements audited by a PRC-licensed certified public accounting firm; there is no turnover, balance-sheet, or headcount exemption for a WFOE. Compulsory audit support is additionally and unconditionally required where: (a) the enterprise is an above-scale industrial enterprise with annual main business revenue of RMB 20 million or more; (b) the CIT annual return includes loss carry-forwards, tax-exempt or reduced income, merger, division, liquidation, or non-resident withholding positions; (c) the WFOE has related-party transactions requiring annual transfer-pricing reporting under SAT Public Notice No. 42 of 2016; (d) the foreign investment annual report discloses an ultimate beneficial owner, cross-border equity pledge, or acquisition of a PRC domestic enterprise; (e) the enterprise applies for bank credit, export tax rebates, or government grants requiring audited financial statements; or (f) the WFOE is placed in liquidation. The audit must be performed in accordance with PRC Standards on Auditing and China Generally Accepted Auditing Standards, using financial statements prepared under PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (PRC CAS, also known as China GAAP), comprising ASBE No. 1 through No. 42 and related interpretations, which are IFRS-converged; small enterprises may elect the Small Enterprise Accounting Standards only if they do not qualify as an above-scale industrial enterprise and do not present public-interest significance, but a WFOE with foreign investment is generally required to maintain full accounts under PRC CAS and produce Chinese-language audited financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For the PRC WFOE, ultimate beneficial controller information is confirmed annually as part of the Enterprise Annual Information Report and the Foreign Investment Information Annual Report filed through the SAMR National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System between 1 January and 30 June. Any shareholding transfer, direct or indirect

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: High and New Technology Enterprise: 15%; Small and Low-Profit Enterprise: effective 5% on annual taxable income up to RMB 3 million (statutory 20% with 75% reduction, extended through 2027); R&D super deduction: 100% additional deduction (200% total deduction); qualified technology transfer income: first RMB 5 million exempt and 50% reduction on the excess; Western Region and Hainan Free Trade Port encouraged-industry incentives may apply at 15% for qualifying manufacturing WFOEs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Corporate Income Tax Annual Return Form A100000, together with supporting schedules A105000, A105050, A105080, A107010 and A107012; filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration Electronic Tax Hall (eTax).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; with quarterly provisional corporate income tax prepayments filed within 15 days after the end of each quarter.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return for the fiscal year ending 31 December must be filed by 31 May of the following calendar year (within 5 months after the fiscal year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales revenue from principal operations (electric cargo e-bikes and step-through scooters).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all worldwide revenue. For export sales to the Hong Kong related party, the invoice price must equal the arm's length price selected under a recognized transfer pricing method; unrealistically low export prices will be adjusted by the State Taxation Administration. Foreign currency amounts are converted at the spot exchange rate on the date of accrual or settlement.

Include direct materials, battery packs, labor, depreciation and manufacturing overhead. Intercompany purchases from the Hong Kong parent must be substantiated with title transfer, import documentation and comparable cost data; non-arm's length purchase prices will be recharacterized.
This is only an accounting subtotal; the tax authority may replace the intercompany gross profit with an arm's length gross profit during a transfer pricing audit.

Deductible taxes include urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, stamp tax and real estate tax; VAT input and output amounts are not deductible for corporate income tax purposes.

Export freight, insurance, advertising and sales commissions are deductible if evidenced and reasonable. Agency or service fees paid to Hong Kong counterparties for selling services must be supported by actual activities, appropriate allocation and arm's length pricing under the benefit test.

Intercompany management fees, IT support and royalties paid to the Hong Kong parent are deductible only where services were actually rendered, allocated on reliable accounting data and priced at arm's length; excessive management fees and passive royalties are a common transfer pricing adjustment.

Interest on related-party debt from Hong Kong shareholders must observe the 2:1 debt-to-equity thin-capitalization ratio and the arm's length interest rate; excessive interest may be reclassified as a dividend and trigger dividend withholding tax.

Start from the board-approved annual financial statements and reconcile the figure with the audited accounts of the WFOE; accounting profit must include all related-party foreign exchange and financing items.

Add back non-deductible costs and unverified invoices; deduct tax-free income, the 100% R&D super deduction, carryforward losses and qualified technology transfer concessions; transfer pricing adjustments and anti-avoidance recharacterizations must be reflected here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable corporate income tax rate and computed tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% statutory rate; 15% is available only if the WFOE holds a valid High and New Technology Enterprise certificate. Quarterly prepayments are summarized and the annual settlement balance is computed.

If the WFOE earns foreign-source income through an overseas branch or investment, creditable foreign tax is capped at the China corporate income tax attributable to that foreign-source income; excess credits may be carried forward for 5 years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable and non-resident dividend withholding obligation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The dividend paid to the Hong Kong shareholder is not taxed to the WFOE, but the WFOE, as withholding agent, must withhold the statutory 10% (or 5% under Mainland-Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement if requirements are met) before remittance and file a separate non-resident withholding tax return through the same eTax portal.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a fine of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000; a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax accrues under the Tax Administration Law Article 32. Understated tax due to false entries or fraudulent declarations is penalized at 50%-500% of underpaid tax under Article 63. If an invoice or expense is fictitious, the criminal tax fraud threshold under Article 201 of the Criminal Law may lead to imprisonment and further economic penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory on gross dividends paid by a China resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise; reduced to 5% under the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement if the beneficial owner is a Hong Kong resident company directly holding at least 25% of the WFOE's share capital.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the 5% dividend rate, the Hong Kong shareholder must submit a certificate of resident status issued by the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department (IR1313A or the applicable English counterpart), a written beneficial ownership declaration, an organizational chart evidencing direct 25%+ holding, board resolutions approving the distribution, audited financial statements, bank payment flows, and evidence of substantive Hong Kong business activity. The WFOE as withholding agent files the treaty-benefit information return through the State Taxation Administration portal under SAT Announcement No. 35/2019 before or at the time of dividend remittance. If beneficial ownership or residency is false, relief is denied and the 10% statutory rate plus late surcharge applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% statutory withholding, 5% under the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA if beneficial ownership and intellectual property substance are established. Interest: 10% statutory withholding, 7% under the DTA for eligible non-PE interest paid to a Hong Kong resident; certain bank interest may be exempt. All treaty reliefs require a Hong Kong tax residence certificate and confirmation that the recipient is the beneficial owner, not a conduit.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Local File is mandatory if annual related-party transactions exceed any of these RMB thresholds: tangible asset transfers above RMB 200 million; financial asset transfers above RMB 100 million; intangible asset transfers above RMB 100 million; other related-party transactions above RMB 40 million. A Master File is required when the Hong Kong parent group's consolidated annual revenue is RMB 5.5 billion or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not maintain an OECD-style Economic Substance Regulations register, but applies substance-over-form, GAAR, CFC rules and anti-treaty-abuse principles. For the WFOE, Core Income-Generating Activities include physical factory production, procurement, inventory management, logistics decisions and risk assumption. For the Hong Kong parent claiming treaty benefits and territorial-source tax exemption, Hong Kong's Foreign-Sourced Income Exemption (FSIE) regime requires substantial economic activity in Hong Kong, including real premises, employees and decision-making; a mailbox entity fails beneficial ownership and CIGA tests and will be denied treaty relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing / Corporate Income Tax Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE sells electric cargo e-bikes to a Hong Kong affiliate at artificially low prices while the affiliate performs no manufacturing, marketing, research or risk functions; excessive royalties and management fees are paid to the HK shell, shifting taxable profit outside mainland China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CIT Law Article 41 and Tax Administration Law Article 63 empower the tax authorities to recharacterize pricing, adjust taxable income, impose overdue interest and levy a penalty of 50%-500% of underpaid tax. Failure to maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation triggers additional fines under SAT Announcement No. 42/2016; criminal tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201 may apply where the underpayment is material.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the legal representative may be jointly and severally liable for restitution under PRC Company Law Article 20; personal bank accounts may be frozen; entry/exit travel blacklisting is imposed under the social credit enforcement regime; criminal conviction under Criminal Law Article 201 carries imprisonment of up to 7 years, fines and confiscation of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent Export VAT Refund / False Trade Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE fabricates export invoices, overstates the FOB value or unit price of electric cargo e-bikes, circulates false Swift_LC or TT_Wire documents, or routes goods through a Hong Kong conduit solely to obtain unwarranted export VAT zero-rating/refund from Chinese customs and tax authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Law Article 204 punishes fraudulent export tax refund with imprisonment of not more than 5 years for relatively large amounts, 5-10 years for huge amounts, and life imprisonment for especially huge or serious cases, plus fines of 1-5 times the defrauded tax. Tax Administration Law Article 66 also imposes a 50%-500% financial penalty and revocation of export-tax privileges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible directors, export manager and legal representative face personal asset confiscation, civil restitution equal to the defrauded refund, criminal imprisonment up to life, passport revocation, exit bans and customs 'blacklisting'; the corporate veil is pierced under PRC Company Law when the corporate form is used to commit fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Treaty Shopping / Shell Company / AML Payment-Rail Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Hong Kong parent company is a mailbox entity with no real office, employees, substantive bank account activity or decision-making; the WFOE routes dividends, interest and royalties through Hong Kong solely to claim the 5% dividend withholding rate and to wash third-party illicit funds through fake trade payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: China's GAAR under CIT Law Article 47 and the anti-abuse/limitation-on-benefits provisions of the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA deny treaty benefits, reinstating 10% statutory withholding; the Anti-Money Laundering Law imposes administrative fines on the entity and responsible persons; Criminal Law Article 191 punishes money laundering with 5-10 years' imprisonment and fines; PRC Company Law Article 20 permits unlimited shareholder and director liability for abuse of limited liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the WFOE and Hong Kong parent are jointly and severally liable for unpaid withholding taxes, interest and civil damages; personal assets are subject to restitution; travel bans and blacklisting prevent cross-border movement; knowing structuring of the conduit flow results in criminal imprisonment for money laundering and ineligibility to serve as a director.
